scan_response.notes: Devices embed their service UUID in scan response data. The app uses CRC-16 mask/pattern matching to filter scan results efficiently: mask = CRC16(prefix + CRC16_of_UUID_bytes) pattern = CRC16(prefix + UUID_bytes_as_little_endian)

device.name: Nuki Smart Lock
device.notes:
The Nuki Smart Lock is a retrofit electronic door lock that mounts over an existing Euro-profile cylinder. It communicates primarily via BLE with an optional WiFi bridge for remote access.
Protocol: encrypted BLE GATT with challenge-response authentication (public key exchange, nonce, authorization IDs). Lock actions are CRC-16 authenticated. All multi-byte values are little-endian.
The app supports multiple Nuki device types (Smart Lock, Opener, Door Sensor, Keypad, Fob, Box, Bridge) each with their own BLE service UUIDs but sharing the same command/response protocol over a GATT data characteristic.
Research status: APK decompiled, full UUID map and command IDs recovered. Message frame format confirmed via BleResponse.java disassembly. Lock state enum and error codes fully enumerated. Pairing/auth flow understood at protocol level from public docs. CRC-16 implementation confirmed (CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE, poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, MSB-first, non-reflected — NOT XModem).
Security: NCC Group's July 2022 advisory disclosed 11 CVEs in Nuki products, including CVE-2022-32507 (broken access controls in the BLE protocol) and CVE-2022-32505 (DoS via unauthenticated BLE packets), fixed in Smart Lock 3.0 FW >=3.3.5 and 2.0 FW >=2.12.4. Official MQTT and Matter-over-Thread APIs are now documented alongside BLE/Web (4th-gen Pro/Ultra/5th-gen support Matter; Ultra/Pro have built-in WiFi, no bridge needed).

issued_to_client: Authorization ID, issued on successful pairing
Lock public key, from the key exchange
credentials.notes: No WiFi passphrase crosses this link — the lock itself is BLE-only, and the separate WiFi bridge handles network credentials on its own. The security PIN is user-chosen and verified over the encrypted channel established by the key exchange.
stored_on_device: Client public keys and their authorization IDs
Security PIN (4-digit on SL 1.0-4.0; 6-digit on Ultra/5th-gen/Go/Pro)

factory_reset.effect: A factory reset exists and clears authorizations, the security PIN and calibration — the lock must be re-taught its door afterwards. The exact button sequence is not established here: it is documented by Nuki per hardware generation and differs between Smart Lock 1.0-4.0 and Pro, and a guessed sequence on a door lock can leave someone locked out of their home. Consult Nuki's documentation for the specific model.

methods.description: Pair over BLE by exchanging public keys, answering the challenge-response, and verifying the security PIN. On success the lock issues an authorization ID that authenticates all later commands.

steps.action: Put the lock into pairing mode by holding its button until the ring LED indicates it is discoverable.
Connect over BLE and discover the keyturner pairing service.
Complete challenge-response authentication (CMD 4: ChallengeResponse, CMD 5: AuthorizationAuthenticatorRequest).
Enter the security PIN (4-digit on SL 1.0-4.0, 6-digit on Ultra/5th-gen/Go/Pro) when the client asks for it.

steps.expect: The lock returns an authorization ID. Store it with the keypair — losing it means re-pairing.

setup.notes:
Unlike most devices in this repo, the Nuki lock genuinely must be provisioned before it will do anything: every command after pairing carries an authorization ID that only the pairing exchange can issue. Pairing is public-key based (CMD 3 PublicKeyRequest, CMD 4/5 challenge-response) and gated by a security PIN the owner sets on first setup — 4 digits on Smart Lock 1.0-4.0, widened to 6 digits with Smart Lock Ultra (6-digit on Ultra/5th-gen/Go/Pro).
The lock is put into pairing mode physically, by holding its button. That is deliberate: it means possession of the door, not proximity to it, is what authorises a new client.
Confidence is medium — the flow is understood from the decompiled app and Nuki's public BLE API documentation, but has not been run against a lock here. Treat the step ordering as documented rather than observed.

rejoin.notes: A previously paired client rejoins with its stored keypair and authorization ID; no reset is needed. A reset is only required to revoke an authorization that can no longer be removed through the app — for example after losing the phone that held it. The optional WiFi bridge is provisioned separately and is not part of this flow.

lock_action.description: Perform a lock/unlock/unlatch/lock-n-go action. Wire format: lockAction u8 + authId u32 + flags u8 + optional 20-byte name suffix + 32-byte nonce (no trigger field — trigger only appears in Keyturner States).
lock_action.name: LockActionRequest / DoorLockActionRequest

set_config.description: Write device configuration (auto-lock timer, button enabled, LED brightness, etc.)
set_config.name: SetConfigRequest

set_security_pin.description: Set or change the security PIN (4 digits on SL 1.0-4.0, 6 digits on Ultra/5th-gen/Go/Pro)
set_security_pin.name: SetSecurityPinRequest

verify_security_pin.description: Verify security PIN to authorize operations
verify_security_pin.name: VerifySecurityPinRequest

crc.notes: MSB-first, non-reflected (NOT the XModem variant — XModem would also imply init 0x0000). Matches the official doc's 'CRC-CCITT, normal (0x1021), initial remainder 0xFFFF' and pyNukiBT's Crc(width=16, poly=0x1021, initvalue=0xffff, reflect_input=False, reflect_output=False). Used on scan response data and message authentication.

lock_actions.5: LOCK_N_GO_WITH_UNLATCH — Lock-n-Go with unlatch at end

lock_states.0: UNCALIBRATED — Lock not yet calibrated, cannot operate
lock_states.252: CALIBRATION — Lock is in calibration mode
lock_states.254: MOTOR_BLOCKED — Motor is blocked, cannot move
lock_states.5: UNLATCHED — Lock is unlatched (door can be pushed open)

message_format.description:
Messages are read from ByteBuffer.wrap(payload).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN). The base BleResponse class defines:
  channel (int, set externally) — routing/message type
  command (short) — command/response identifier
  payload — variable-length, command-specific data

pairing.description: Nuki uses public-key based pairing with challenge-response authentication: 1. BLE connection and service discovery 2. Public key exchange (CMD 3: PublicKeyRequest / PublicKeyResponse) 3. Challenge-response authentication (CMD 4: ChallengeResponse, CMD 5: AuthorizationAuthenticatorRequest) 4. Security PIN verification (CMD 32: VerifySecurityPinRequest) 5. On success, the device returns an authorization ID used for subsequent commands

nuki_specific.authorization_id: Integer ID assigned after successful pairing, used to authenticate all commands
nuki_specific.security_pin: Numeric PIN set during initial setup: 4 digits (uint16) on Smart Lock 1.0-4.0, 6 digits (uint32) on Ultra/5th-gen/Go/Pro
